summary:
I've been generating art for Keikochō, a Japanese-learning app I build for myself, and spent a chunk of this cycle on the pipeline that turns prompts into pictures rather than the app itself. I moved image generation from a local Stable Diffusion box to Replicate, and the switch quietly broke something for weeks: the style prompt and negative bans that keep the art PG and consistent were wired into the local path only, so every image made on Replicate went out with none of them applied. Traced it, fixed the plumbing, then ran an A/B across ~140 test images to map out which model handles which kind of scene — one model is reliable for a person standing somewhere, useless for two people having a conversation; a different model can't render booru-style tags at all but is the only one that can count objects correctly, so "seven balls in a row" needed its own prompt logic to stop the model from rounding to a tidy grid of six or nine.

Also caught a caching bug that made regenerated art invisible after deploy — the server wasn't sending cache headers and the service worker cached images as if they never changed, so replacing a picture on disk did nothing in the browser until I split the caching strategy into immutable assets versus content that's expected to change.

On the automation side (Hermes, the agent I run at home) I fixed a case where a background job left a process-wide flag set after it finished, so every subsequent request quietly got treated as a scheduled job instead of a live one — the kind of bug that doesn't crash anything, it just makes the system politely refuse to do what you asked, which took some digging through logs to catch since nothing errors.

highlights.oneLiner: Moved Keikochō image gen from local SD to Replicate; fixed style prompts not reaching it, A/B'd ~140 images across models
Fixed a stuck process-wide cron flag that made every request silently get treated as scheduled
